segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics News Digest for November 16, 2026.
We've got 14 updates, including Gemini's new dexterity, OpenAI's shift in focus, and DHL's warehouse AI pilots.
Tune in for the latest.
From Robotics & Automation News, Google DeepMind launches Gemini Robotics 2.5 with improved dexterity and industrial capabilities.
This report details the release of an updated vision-language-action model designed to enhance robots' capacity for complex physical tasks through advancements in dexterity, reliability, and safety.
The new model demonstrated success rates 30 to 100 percent higher and completed operations 20 to 30 percent faster across more than two hundred tasks.
Demonstrations included the Apptronik Apollo 2 humanoid robot successfully executing automotive kitting operations on Mercedes-Benz production lines.
Safety enhancements were incorporated through new controls that increased safe task completion around obstacles and personnel.
Furthermore, the development incorporated ASIMOV-Jailbreak and utilized the Gemini 4 Argon model to generate training scenarios, thereby accelerating robotics research.
This advancement signals a significant step forward in integrating advanced AI into practical industrial automation.
From Humanoid.guide, "OpenAI disbands robotics team, folds work into core research".
This report details OpenAI's restructuring of its robotics focus by integrating the team's work into core research and applied organizations following a shift in research methodology.
The company determined that general purpose frontier models can be directly applied to robotics, leading to the dissolution of the specialized robotics team.
This restructuring reflects a move away from a separate development approach toward leveraging existing large models for robotics tasks.
OpenAI is now focusing development internally on a humanoid robot, with a target for a public demonstration in 2027.
This development challenges the premise that robotics requires entirely separate model development.
The implications suggest that general intelligence models can augment real-world robot experience.
Industry focus will now be on the practical application and integration of advanced models in physical systems.
From Robotics & Automation News, "DHL Supply Chain pilots adaptive robotics and AI orchestration in warehouse operations".
This report details DHL Supply Chain's initiative to coordinate robotics, artificial intelligence, and human workers across its global logistics network through an Intelligent Supply Chain framework.

Adaptive robots are being utilized to adjust their actions based on changing conditions, supported by AI orchestration software that connects employees, equipment, and data to coordinate entire warehouse workflows.
The testing involved systems dynamically allocating resources according to order volumes to enhance throughput and flexibility.
This approach integrates physical AI controlling machinery with digital AI analyzing information to foster an efficient and resilient supply chain with human expertise.
This development signals a trend toward holistic operational management in logistics driven by integrated physical and digital intelligence.
From Robotics & Automation News, Zacua Ventures raised $135 million for its second fund focusing on robotics, physical AI, and industrial technologies, marking a significant expansion of investment.
This fund more than doubled the original fifty-six million dollar fund and attracted commitments from over thirty investors across the globe.
The firm is broadening its investment focus beyond construction to encompass the broader Physical Industries including manufacturing and energy sectors.
Zacua has already deployed investments in companies such as Gravis Robotics and Origin Robotics, illustrating a clear interest in industrial automation.
The firm utilizes its established network to grant portfolio companies access to industrial customers and operational testing environments.
This investment signals increased capital flow into tangible automation and physical artificial intelligence applications across heavy industry.
From Robotics & Automation News, Avride reaches one million robot deliveries as network expands across US.
This report details the company's milestone of one million robot deliveries accomplished through the expansion of its network into urban neighborhoods and university campuses.
In October, Avride reported eighteen thousand deliveries, and the system currently manages a daily volume of seven thousand deliveries.
The operation spans over thirty United States markets, including metropolitan areas such as Austin and Miami.
These robotic units interface with existing food delivery platforms like Uber Eats and Grubhub to facilitate customer ordering.
Growth in delivery volume is credited to coordination between internal teams and commercial partners, with further expansion planned.
This development indicates continued integration of autonomous systems into consumer logistics infrastructure.
From Robotics & Automation News, Wing and Walmart launch drone delivery service in Memphis.

This report details the initiation of an autonomous drone delivery service utilizing partnerships between Wing and Walmart in the Memphis area, establishing drone delivery for groceries and essentials from Walmart with delivery times as fast as thirty minutes.

The initial service deployment covers neighborhoods surrounding Walmart Supercenters located in Bartlett, Cordova, and West Memphis, marking an expansion of autonomous delivery into Tennessee and Arkansas.
The system employs drones capable of speeds up to sixty miles per hour, designed to provide a practical alternative for time-sensitive purchases.
This development is part of a broader strategy to reach nearly twenty U.S. metropolitan areas by the year two thousand twenty-seven.
The ongoing expansion indicates continued integration of aerial robotics into commercial logistics operations.
From Robotics & Automation News, Serve Robotics opens autonomous delivery network to developers and businesses.
This report details the launch of an Autonomous Vehicle Delivery Developer Portal, which enables programmatic summoning of robots from the autonomous sidewalk delivery fleet.
The platform incorporates a public application programming interface and a testing sandbox environment designed for developers to test applications before deploying on live robots.
This system allows applications, businesses, and artificial intelligence assistants to integrate these robots for tasks such as last-mile delivery through the platform.
Serve Robotics manages the intricate operations including dispatch, routing, navigation, and supervision for all deliveries.
This innovation seeks to establish affordable on-demand delivery by integrating physical robotics into routine workflows.
The development signals a broader integration path for physical robotics within commercial service applications.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Dyna-2.1!".

This report details the introduction of Dyna-2.1, a software foundation model for robotics developed by DYNA Robotics in California, which has achieved a Humanoid Guide Brain Score of eight out of ten, placing it within the state of the art band.
The model resides within the intelligence layer of a robotic system, setting it apart from physical hardware.
A scheduled release date for Dyna-2.1 is September 29, 2026, and the product is presently available on backorder.
Prospective purchasers are advised to evaluate the software's performance based on specific deployment requirements rather than mechanical specifications.
This development indicates progression in the intelligence layer of robotic systems and points toward evolving benchmarks in artificial intelligence for robotics.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, GR RL!".

This segment reports on GR RL, a robot foundation model developed by ByteDance Seed that addresses the challenge of noisy human demonstrations by combining demonstration training with reinforcement learning through subsequent robot practice.
The training process involves three stages: filtering poor demonstrations, mirroring retained examples, and introducing practice guided by results.
This research focuses on refining the methods for training robot policies rather than producing a physical robot product.
The model is assessed as developing, reflecting its focus on the quality of learning methods within robotics.
This advancement indicates a focus on improving the learning methodologies underpinning artificial intelligence in robotics.
Further developments in robotic learning algorithms are anticipated.
From Robotics & Automation News, "GITEX Global to showcase latest humanoid robots and physical AI technologies in Dubai".
This report details the upcoming GITEX World RobotiX event in Dubai, which will focus on humanoid robots and physical artificial intelligence technologies.
The exhibition, scheduled from December 8 to 11, will feature demonstrations from companies including Unitree and Lumos Robotics, alongside various autonomous systems.
The showcase emphasizes the increasing interest in physical AI, driven by recent advancements in computing hardware and software for robotics.
Numerous organizations will present products demonstrating applications across industrial automation, security, and consumer goods, incorporating educational demonstrations of AI development tools.
This event signals continued integration of physical AI into practical commercial applications.
From Humanoid.guide, LG partners with KIRIA on humanoid safety before 2027 debut.
This story concerns a collaboration aimed at developing safety, reliability, and usability assessments for humanoid robots prior to their planned 2027 introduction.
LG Electronics and KIRIA are jointly developing testing infrastructure and contributing to national and international safety standards at KIRIA's Humanoid Robot Safety Certification Center.
This partnership focuses on identifying critical challenges such as collision avoidance and motion stability for robots operating in shared human spaces through rigorous verification efforts.
The process involves LG integrating hardware, intelligence, and operational data into its robotics program to ensure safety compliance.
This safety verification effort directly supports LG's development of a bipedal robot scheduled for unveiling in early 2027.
The work establishes a framework for regulatory oversight in the evolving humanoid robotics sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, Robbyant launches LingBot-Touch to give robots a sense of touch.
This story details the release of an open-source tactile foundation model that unifies magnetic, visual, and piezoresistive sensing to enable robots to perceive touch.
The LingBot-Touch architecture translates these diverse sensor signals into a shared fingertip coordinate space, facilitating shared tactile understanding across different hands and action models.

Integration of this model resulted in substantial performance enhancements, with action models demonstrating gains ranging from fourteen to twenty-six percentage points in real-world manipulation tasks.
The model is engineered for reusability across various sensors and dexterous hands, accommodating future hardware evolution.
This development signals a significant step toward more nuanced and adaptable robotic interaction capabilities.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Runtime governability in ROS 2: where should changing operating conditions be handled?".

This story examines the architectural considerations for managing shifts in external operating conditions within active ROS 2 systems, focusing on where this dynamic context should be represented and evaluated.

The discussion explored whether existing ROS 2 lifecycle management mechanisms are sufficient and investigated potential locations for context representation, including the task layer, a supervisory component, or external services.

Specific inquiries addressed context ownership, the handling of source unavailability, and the introduction of higher-level logic while maintaining local safety guarantees, centering on the concept of runtime governability in autonomous systems.
This research provides guidance for designing more robust and adaptable autonomous software architectures.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Why Skydio Built a Lopsided Drone".
This story details the engineering process behind the Skydio F10 Lightrunner, which is a fixed-wing camera drone featuring asymmetrical wings designed to accommodate a wingtip camera payload.
Engineers achieved this design through modeling and optimization to balance the camera, lift, and control requirements, necessitating uneven motor placement to counteract the increased drag.

The system utilizes model predictive control to autonomously manage transitions between hovering and high-speed flight, and it incorporates a MegaDock system for the autonomous management of up to five drones.
This work demonstrates advanced control methods for complex aerodynamic systems.
Future developments in autonomous aerial systems will likely build upon these advancements in control and payload integration.
And that’s all the circuits for today!
Hope your day is as smoothly programmed as Gemini Robotics 2.5.
Until tomorrow, keep those algorithms humming!
Bye for now!
